# **Motivation**

***

This case study explores working with spatially-informed gene expression data, also known as {{< glossary "Spatial Transcriptomics" display="Spatial Transcriptomics (ST)" >}}, to explore {{< glossary "Differential Gene Expression" display="differential gene expression" >}}.

:::{.definition_box}
::::{.definition_box_header}
Differential Gene Expression
::::
::::{.inner_block}
The difference in expression of a gene between samples or cases. Differential expression is typically thought of as a difference in abundance or amount of expression, but may also be a difference in what cell types a gene is expressed in or where a gene is expressed spatially within a tissue.
::::
:::

Spatial Transcriptomic methods produce data that allow for gene expression to be investigated and described within a spatial context. 

:::{.definition_box}
::::{.definition_box_header}
Spatial Transcriptomics
::::
::::{.inner_block}
Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) refers to molecular methods used to measure gene expression at or near single-cell resolution, reporting where observed transcripts are physically located within the source tissue, preserving spatial context.
::::
:::

In this way, researchers can explore where a gene is expressed within a tissue and how that may change over time, based on experimental conditions, or for different clinical contexts. Spatial transcriptomics is a rapidly-evolving area of development that can be used for {{< glossary "Hypothesis generation" display = "hypothesis generation" >}} for a variety of biological questions such as describing cell neighborhoods, cell-cell interactions, and discovering biomarkers or drug targets. 


```{r, echo = FALSE, fig.align = 'center', out.width = "100%", fig.alt = "Illustration showing the uses of spatial transcriptomics, underlining that it is largely used to generate hypotheses, desciribing cell neighborhoods and cell interactions as well as discovering biomarkers or niche interface processes. It can complement results from single cell RNA seq and be integrated with images for deeper understanding."}

```

Platforms or technologies to generate spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are typically categorized as either sequencing-based or image-based. Both types will provide researchers with spatially-informed gene expression data, however one type allows researchers to investigate the whole transcriptome while the other is limited to a specified set of genes called a panel. Inversely, the ones that investigate the whole transcriptome typically have to deconvolve multicellular spots to estimate single-cell data while the ones that investigate a limited set of genes have a single-cell or sub-cellular view of expression and instead must segment the data into discrete cell [@Lim_Wang_Buzdin_Li_2025]. Often researchers will use complementary spatial transcriptomic approaches to study the impacts of (ex: @Kwon_etal_2026). The technologies and their trade-offs will be described in more detail in the [Context](https://www.opencasestudies.org/ocs-bio-spatial-transcriptomics/#context) section of the case study.

In this case study, we will use `spatialGE`, an R tool [@Ospina_Wilson_Soupir_Berglund_Smalley_Tsai_Fridley_2022], to work with image-based spatial transcriptomics data [@Kwon_etal_2026], specifically focusing on: 

* The data that is produced by the image-based platform.
* Importing the data .
* Inspecting and working with a `spatialGE` object that stores the data.
* Performing quality control and filtering out low quality or irrelevant data.
* Transforming or normalizing the image-based data to account for technical artifacts [@Atta_Clifton_Anant_Aihara_Fan_2024].
* Creating data visualizations known as {{< glossary "Quilt plot" display="Quilt plots" >}} to visualize spatial patterns of gene expression.
* Annotating cells within the dataset, exploring cell type specific spatial patterns of gene expression.

Downstream analyses for more global and statistical summaries of spatial patterns will be introduced but not shown in-depth within this case study.

***
